title: fix(console): the docs portal's book sidebar keeps a doc placed by its own `group` key from outside the book's package (objectui#11245)
body:
Fixes #11245
Clause-②: no

## What

`scopeDocsToBook` in `apps/console/src/pages/book-nav.ts` now keeps a doc whose own `group` names one of the book's group keys, whatever package the doc lives in. Everything else about the scoping step is unchanged. When the book declares a package, docs from other packages are still dropped before resolving, so they never reach the synthetic Uncategorized group or an `include` rule. `include` is still scoped by the local `resolveBookTree` port itself, to `group.package` or else the book's package. `resolveBookTree`, `homeBook` and the direct-route refusal are not touched. There is no new helper. `DocPage.tsx`, `BookPage.tsx` and `countBookDocs` pick up the fix through the helper they already call.

## Why

The spec's `resolveBookTree` (`packages/spec/src/system/book.zod.ts` in objectstack, byte-identical at the `@objectstack/spec@17.5.0` tag this repo installs and on objectstack `main`) places a doc in a group by `d.group === group.key` with no package scope. `GET /meta/book/:name/tree` answers that resolver over every doc (`createMetaBookTreeAnswer` → `readableTree`, with `bookPackage = book._packageId`). The portal dropped the doc before resolving, so a doc an admin placed from the doc editor was listed by the endpoint and missing from the sidebar.

## Measured (the order's Zone 2)

These readings come from a scratch suite that ran the port and the spec resolver on the same fixtures. The suite was not committed.

1. **Red first.** Before the fix, through `scopeDocsToBook` → port, the book gave `start=[docprobe_gs_welcome] reference=[]`. The spec resolver on the endpoint's inputs gave `reference=[live_guide,probe_curl]`. After the fix the two agree.
2. **The port's own scope. The PM's assumption is partly falsified.** With the scope passed and no pre-filter, the port matches the spec on the explicit-`group` leg. But neither the port nor the spec scopes the orphan catch-all. Both put another package's ungrouped doc into Uncategorized: `uncategorized=[other_note]` from each. So "stop pre-filtering and pass the scope" would break the ruled control. The fix therefore keeps the pre-filter and lets explicit members through it, as the ruling words it: "`scopeDocsToBook` keeps any doc whose `group` names one of the book's group keys". The portal's scoped Uncategorized is a deliberate, ruled narrowing of the endpoint's. The pins compare the **authored** groups with the spec's answer.
3. **Group-level `package` override.** In both resolvers the override **replaces** the book's scope for that group's `include`; it does not add to it. Fixture: `own` gets only package a, `ext` gets package b through `include` plus c_1 through its own `group`. The portal's answer equals the spec's, and one pin holds it.
4. **`homeBook` / `findBookContainingDoc`.** Nothing changes for a book that carries a stamped `packageId`. `homeBook` keeps only books of the doc's own package, and that package is already in scope for them. One edge case moves. The book must carry no stamped `packageId`, its name prefix must equal the doc's package, and its only package must be a group `package` override. If such a doc names one of that book's groups, it is now claimed by that book. `homeBook` then answers that book instead of the package's first book (the measured fixture moved from `q_other` to `q_manual`). That follows `homeBook`'s documented rule (the home is the book that claims the doc), and `homeBook` was not changed.

Divergences beyond the explicit-`group` leg, reported and not widened:
- **An unstamped doc under a scoped `include`.** The spec admits a doc with no `packageId` into any scoped `include`. The port falls back to the name prefix (`pkgOf`) and refuses it. Measured: port `all=[x_a]`, spec `all=[x_a,y_unstamped]`.
- **A `pages` pin naming a doc from another package.** The pre-filter drops that doc's header, so the entry keeps its place but loses its label and description. Measured: port `{"doc":"c_9"}`, spec `{"doc":"c_9","label":"C9 Label"}`.

## Tests

- `book-nav.explicitGroup-11245.test.ts`: the explicit member is listed in the group it names; the authored groups equal the spec resolver's answer (`@objectstack/spec/system`) for the same docs; `countBookDocs` counts it; the group-override case; control: another package's ungrouped doc, and one naming a key the book lacks, stay out, with no Uncategorized.
- `docs-portal.explicitGroup-11245.test.tsx` renders through the real route table. The Reference group of the rendered sidebar links the placed doc, and marks it current when reading it. A book whose only member is placed that way opens to it instead of "This book has no documents yet". Control: another package's ungrouped doc is absent from the sidebar.
- **Reverse verification**, run from the committed fix through `ablation-replace.mjs` with a disk-verified mutation and restore:
  - Drop the explicit-member leg: 7 of the 9 new tests go red and both controls stay green.
  - Drop the package filter entirely: both new controls go red, plus three existing `docs-portal.test.tsx` cases (that is the existing pin the triage names).
  - Each restore was proven by blob equal to HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

Gate verdicts and the head they ran on are in the `os-dev-report` comment on the card.

## Acceptance notes

- `homeBook` edge case (reading 4 above): the canonical URL moves for a doc placed into an own-package book that has no stamped `packageId` and a group-level `package` override.
- The two port divergences above: `pkgOf` falls back to the name prefix on an unstamped doc, and a `pages` pin from another package loses its label. Carrier: none.
- A common group key such as `reference` places a doc in every book that has a group with that key. The spec resolver and the tree endpoint do the same; the pins do not cover it.
